channel.title: Oleksandr Shepotylo
channel.description: Development, institutions, and spatial economics — work outside the four main hubs.

item.title: Spatial spillovers in the development of institutions
item.description:
Institutional quality in one country is not independent of institutional quality next door: reform and dysfunction both spread across borders. We develop a spatial econometric framework to estimate these cross-country spillovers directly, rather than treating each country’s institutions as determined purely by its own history and policy choices.

Published in: Journal of Development Economics, 101(C), 297–315

item.title: Cities in Transition
item.description:
Post-socialist cities inherited industrial geographies built for central planning, not markets. This paper tracks how urban economic structure in transition countries evolved after 1991 — which cities adapted, which stayed locked into declining industries, and what that implies for regional policy.

Published in: Comparative Economic Studies, 54(3), 661–688

item.title: Spatial complementarity of FDI: the example of transition countries
item.description:
Foreign direct investment into one transition country raises, rather than diverts, FDI into its neighbours — the opposite of the substitution effect that simple location-competition models predict. We show FDI flows into this region are spatial complements, most plausibly through shared supply chains and demonstration effects on investor perceptions of the wider region.

Published in: Post-Communist Economies, 24(3), 327–349
